mega_048__mega_026.study_setting: US online participants in the Strengthening Democracy Challenge were randomized to scalable interventions intended to reduce anti-democratic and hostile partisan attitudes. The two conditions used very different formats: a short article versus an eight-minute guided audio meditation.
mega_048__mega_026.outcome_measure: The archive's post-treatment anti-democratic-attitudes (ADA) index from the Strengthening Democracy Challenge, coded in the source analysis so that higher values indicate fewer anti-democratic attitudes (greater support for democratic norms).
mega_048__mega_026.condition_a_material: Participants read an article arguing that the American democratic system is distinctive because people generally do not turn on one another and remain faithful to civility and respect through recessions, pandemics, and natural disasters. It acknowledged political debate and media outlets that inflate differences, but argued that Americans retain faith in the system and trust in one another, with a majority committed to mutual respect. This is the submitters' detailed protocol description; the full article text was not included in the static archive.
mega_048__mega_026.condition_b_material: Participants listened to an eight-minute befriending meditation emphasizing kindness to oneself and others. It guided them to wish safety, happiness, health, and ease first for themselves, then for a loved one, a stranger, someone they find difficult, and finally all living beings. This is the submitters' detailed protocol description; the audio transcript was not included in the static archive.
